Requirement: Reload keeps same webContents ID but does not preserve session/consent state
Scenario: Real attach + proposeWrite + issueWriteConsent, then win.reload() (real packaged renderer reload)
ExpectedResult: webContentsId unchanged (Electron behavior); stale proposal/consent rejected; stale attach/session rejected
ResidualRisk: Electron does not change webContents.id on reload — only navigation/JS state resets. Session/consent rejection was verified via the MAIN-PROCESS side (replaying the stale proposal/consent after reload), not merely inferred from the renderer's own JS state being cleared

Requirement: No freeze resumes automatically after reload
Scenario: Not separately exercised this cycle (Phase 6 used the write flow
column12: The session-teardown mechanism (beginCleanupRevocation / disposeSession) is not reload-specific — it is keyed to render-process-gone and explicit detach, not 'reload'. A renderer reload does NOT itself trigger session disposal (only crash/detach/quit do, per electron/main.ts's render-process-gone and will-quit handlers) — the CORRECT expected behavior may be that a reload alone does not tear down the session at all (unlike crash), meaning the real security boundary here is the stale-artifact rejection already proven (proposalId/consentToken are per-operation, not per-session), not a reload-specific session teardown. Flagged as an architecture clarification, not a defect, but not independently re-verified against a fresh reload-specific session-teardown assertion this cycle.

Requirement: Main-window close and recreation without inherited authority
Scenario: Not separately exercised this cycle as a distinct in-process scenario
Status: PENDING — architecturally not a real Windows code path
ResidualRisk: On Windows, app.on('window-all-closed') calls app.quit() unconditionally (process.platform !== 'darwin' check) — there is no 'close main window, keep app running, recreate it' state in this packaged app's real behavior. The only window-recreation code path (app.on('activate') -> createWindow() if mainWindow===null) is a macOS-only-reachable Electron boilerplate remnant that a real Windows user can never trigger through normal interaction. The functionally equivalent real scenario — close window -> app quits -> app relaunches -> createWindow() runs again -> no old authority survives — is already fully covered by Phase 4.1-4.5's shutdown-and-restart proofs. Not independently re-tested via a synthetic app.emit('activate') call this cycle; documented as an architecture-driven scope narrowing rather than attempted and faked.

Requirement: Same-prefix path attack / encoded path variation / Windows case behavior / directory traversal (9.2-9.5)
ResidualRisk: The packaged app's trusted URL prefix is a single file:// URL pointing at the app's own asar-bundled dist/index.html (registered once at window creation, electron/main.ts:255-258) — there is no sibling directory or case-variant path within the packaged app's own asar to construct a realistic same-prefix or traversal attack against without fabricating an artificial second app installation. The underlying validateTrustedSender check performs an isMainFrame check plus prefix validation against that fixed registered prefix list — the logical boundary (child-frame rejection, non-matching prefix rejection) is exercised by 9.1/9.6 above; the specific encoded-path/traversal sub-cases were not separately reproduced against a realistic target this cycle.

column12: validateIpcSender's isMainFrame check (electron/sender-validation.ts:48) structurally rejects any non-main-frame sender for every privileged handler that calls it — this is a per-handler, non-bypassable code path, not a per-scenario configuration. Constructing a live child-iframe inside the packaged renderer to exercise this at runtime (rather than by code inspection) was not attempted this cycle; DevTools is not enabled in this packaged build by design (production candidate) and enabling it solely for this test would itself be a scope violation of the authorization ('Do not enable DevTools in the normal production build solely for testing').
